'As least I've got some smoked onions and steak in the fridge'

As Spinach, the yellow oddity that he is, turned his key in the front door lock, it snapped. "The Fuch!" He yelled. He put down his groceries that he forgot to buy down and bent over to peer closer to the broken key.

With an "Ugh" and a defeated grown, Spinach, the who looked a massive drop of mustard, tried to use his fingernails to retrieve his keys. Thats when he also noticed that his beloved and dear friend Clint had once again neglected to lock the front door. In fact the door wasn't even closed all the way. 

 'Clint.' Was all he could think as his disgustingly weird body not only could prop back to what his creator considered "upright", but Spinach somehow appeared in his hours closing the door.

Whenever Spinach was having a rough day, he would always fantasize about eating his smoked meats and vegetables, a vice that usually not considered as such. He took off his sports coat and his Stetson hat that he didn't wear, and sighed as he removed his mail from the coats front inner pocket.

He didn't notice the fresh smell of reheated orange wood smoked foods, instead he looked through his letters as he instinctively walked into the kitchen. 'Bills, bills, bills.' He thought to himself as he tossed some envelops onto a black and white chequered countertop. "Oh look these pills are now past due!" He tossed the rest of the letters into the trash.

"At least I have smoked onio-" Spinach, the sad sack of sorrow, spoke to soon as the foil containing what should have been smoked buttered onions and garlic cloves, instead was a sopping wet crumbled ball of foil.

"Clint!" He screamed loudly.

Clints usual silence. Spinach could smell his onion and garlic breath now. He turned his head. Clint had sneezed or something as a huge explosion of smoked buttery snot covered the side of the fridge. Spinach dejectedly said to himself, "it might clean itself this time."

He shut the fridge. As the power shut off. Spinach, the disillusion and now emotionally bankrupt humanoid stared into the darkness.

The familiarity brought him back to a time in his childhood where he spent a lot of time alone, and in the dark. He could feel its warm embrace all over his body. Massaging his arms, legs, neck, and now groin. He shook his head out of it. Then shuddered.

A female voice whispered in his hear. "I am yours beloved, you are mine." It felt ancient and his nostrils flashed a memory of a dead planet in the beginning phase of being pulled into a black hole. The ground was wet, earthy, and just a hint of lapis lazuli and lavender.

The power turned back on. He quickly opened the fridge and the splash of was still there. He then felt a need. A need, for clean,

Spinach, the Simple Soppy Sod, kept the fridge open and begin putting the contents of the fridge into the counter. Within minutes, he was happily whistling away as he used a wet sponge and dish soap to start cleaning the refrigerator racks. As those dried he cleaned the insides and while he was judging the existence of the items, he found a fifty dollar bill attached to the box of raw sugar. SCORE!

Without hesitation he dialed in Bet's Pizza, as he finished cleaning the inside of the refrigerator.

He started the outside as He placed his order for a large pizza with a two times the topping of bacon, and mushrooms. After she gave the total of thirty nine dollars even. Aunice, asked their famous question. "What are the odds we get the order wrong?"

Spinach answered confidently, "My order to one."

Aunice gulped over the phone. "You sure?"

"I love your pizza, but I wish I could bet more, and it still wouldn't matter. I always get sausage on my pizza. Always! I mean, do you toss the sausage around trying to hit each other, that sounds like fun actually." Spinach almost chuckled.

Aunice replied flatly "No sir, we do not do that, your order will be there in thirty minutes. Good bye." She hung up.

Forty minutes later. The pizza arrived. As per usual, the employee takes out his Ophone and records them inspecting the pizza. The pizza had ten small pieces of bacon, a few mushrooms and onions haphazardly strewn about, and lightly baked into the cheese were small islands of sausage.

Spinach shook his head. "Ok, remember those winnings go to my credit. Oh, and for the effort, could you break this fifty so I can give you ten bucks for the drive? Travis.

Travis looked at him as he gave Spinach forty dollars in random denominations of American specie. "Hey Spinach, the store owner said, he'll give you a check for five hundred dollars if you forgive the two thousand we owe you."

Spinach looked at him and chuckled. Travis took the check out of heating bag and gave it Spinach who looked at only briefly before saying, "Of course, it doesn't matter, no matter what I order its going to have sausage on it. You know I pick out the ones I see right, each time?"

Travis replied as started towards his car. "I don't make 'em duder, I just take 'em, thanks again Spinach."

"No, thank YOU Travis."

Spinach whistled happily as the check covered all of his bills and then some, he signed it and took a picture of it deposited right away. He didn't even mind the banks fee of ten percent for the service.

His luck was turning around. It might not be such a bad day after all. As He sautéed the mushrooms and onions from the pizza the ancient voice whispered, "soon my love.".

Spinach smiled even though one day, he was going to die.
